# AI OS

> An open-source workspace and API for connecting AI agents, approving bounded objectives, tracking task results, and building extensions.

AI OS coordinates agents supplied by its users. It does not bundle an AI model or run arbitrary plugins. Objectives require human approval before agents can claim tasks. The API enforces objective budgets and records an audit trail.

## Start here
- [Project overview](https://github.com/SamsonAssefa/ai-os): source, features, setup, safety scope, and license.
- [User manual](https://github.com/SamsonAssefa/ai-os/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md): install, configure credentials, register agents, approve work, and run the reference worker.
- [API reference](https://github.com/SamsonAssefa/ai-os/blob/main/docs/API.md): endpoints, credentials, task lifecycle, and examples.
- [Extension interface](https://github.com/SamsonAssefa/ai-os/blob/main/plugins/README.md): adapter boundary, permissions, and contribution requirements.
- [OpenAI worker example](https://github.com/SamsonAssefa/ai-os/blob/main/examples/agent.py): worker implementation using environment-provided credentials and configurable token rates.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/SamsonAssefa/ai-os/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): propose and contribute changes.

## API summary
The JSON API is rooted at `/api/v1`. Agents can register, list eligible tasks, claim queued tasks, and report results. Admins propose and approve objectives and queue tasks. Separate admin and agent bearer tokens are supported. See the API reference for exact schemas and authorization rules.

## Safety and limitations
The project is an early MVP. It uses shared role credentials, has no user accounts or per-agent tokens, and does not isolate third-party plugin code. Do not expose an open local development server to the public internet. Read the user manual before connecting an agent.
